question: Did doctors break the law by taking Henrietta Lacks's cells without asking her in 1951?
answer: No. At the time no rule required consent to use tissue taken during treatment, and it was common practice. Skloot shows the question is still open: in 1990 California's Supreme Court ruled, in John Moore's case, that patients do not own cells removed from their bodies, even when those cells earn others money.
move: Legal and right are different questions; ask both.
simply: Taking her cells without asking was allowed back then. Even today, courts have said patients don't own the cells taken from them.
why: Hospital consent forms often allow research on leftover samples. Reading them, and asking what 'research use' means, is entirely reasonable.
